title: Process Communication
body:
Same thing as [[Inter-process Communication]]; that note owns the material. Two names for
one topic, kept apart here only because both appear in the course notes.

**Go to [[Inter-process Communication]]** for the taxonomy: the two forms are
[[Shared Memory]] and [[Message Passing]], and everything else ([[Piping]], [[FIFO]],
sockets, signals) is one of those two wearing a different interface.

The one distinction worth drawing while you are here, because the words invite the mistake:

| Between | How they talk | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Two [[Thread\|threads]] in one process | already share the address space; just write a global | free, and every write is a race you must lock ([[Critical Section]]) |
| Two processes | need IPC, because their address spaces are separate | a [[System Call]] and usually a copy |

Threads communicating is not IPC at all: nothing is *inter*-process about it. That is the
whole reason threads are cheap and the whole reason they are dangerous.
